before.title: Supplement: Latest developments in memory and Context Engineering
before.content:
Supplement: Latest developments in memory and Context Engineering
History summarization (compaction) and file-based memory are now API features. Both still just save and re-inject; that part has not changed.
What changed
Item
Update
Date
Automatic compaction
API that summarizes history on the server, released in beta
2026/2/5
Compaction at any point
The application decides when to summarize. Images and documents in the summarized range are lost
Beta 2026/9/14
Memory tool
The model requests file operations; the application executes them in its own storage. Beta flag no longer needed
2026/2/17
Link to the lecture: Of the three scopes, compaction compresses “history within the loop”; the memory tool covers “records across sessions.” Weights don't change.
Caveats: The application owns the storage. The docs require validating paths outside it. Instructions lost in a summary no longer apply.
Source: Anthropic “Claude Platform release notes” (2026/2/5, 2/17, 9/14), “Memory tool”, docs on compaction at any point (the latter two undated). Information checked: 2026/10/9

before.title: Without memory, every session starts from scratch
before.content:
Without memory, every session starts from scratch
If you ask “Fix the failing test” again the next day, can the agent reuse the cause it identified before?
Source: Based on Luo et al., “From Storage to Experience,” arXiv:2605.06716 (2026/5/7, ACL 2026 Findings), §1 and §3.2; Ding et al., “Always-On Agents,” arXiv:2606.30306 (2026/6/29); Anthropic, “Compaction overview” (Claude Platform Docs, accessed 2026/10/21).
1
Starting from scratch
Re-explaining past
decisions
2
Repeating mistakes
Re-investigating causes
found last time
3
Long tasks get cut off
Context limit drops
intermediate progress
Storing everything brings back old info and errors too. Design what to keep and what to discard.

before.title: Example: Claude
before.content:
Example: Claude
An example in Claude: some mechanisms work within a session, while others work across sessions
Source: Anthropic, “Compaction overview” and “Memory tool” (Claude Platform Docs); “How Claude remembers your project” (Claude Code Docs); all accessed 2026/10/21. Packer et al. (2023), arXiv:2310.08560.
Inside the context (same session)
Compaction (summarize history to fit)
Replaces old history with a summary.
External storage (across sessions)
Memory tool (Claude API)
The model requests operations on files in /memories;
the application executes them in its own storage
Auto memory (Claude Code)
Claude writes its own notes and
loads the first 200 lines or 25KB each time
Write out
The agent reads it back when needed
Stored memory enters the next context. A human checks its contents.
There is also a risk of writes from outside.

before.title: Example: OpenClaw
before.content:
Example: OpenClaw
Every night, it rereads past conversations and moves only what to keep into long-term memory.
Source: OpenClaw Docs, “Memory overview” and “Memory architecture,” as of 2026/10. Stage descriptions are summarized.
Daily notes (memory/<date>.md)
Notes from 10/24
Notes from 10/25
Notes from 10/26
Nightly, automatic
Review (dreaming)
1 Collect: drop duplicates, and list candidates
2 Compare: find recurring themes
3 Move: keep only what passes the threshold
MEMORY.md (long-term memory)　Loaded at the start of the next session
No manual cleanup needed
Not everything is kept
One-off lookups stay only in daily notes, so long-term memory doesn't bloat.

before.title: Memory
before.content:
Memory
Context is finite. When starting a new chat, we want a system that can refer to past context.
Source: Schematic for illustration. Where it is stored (files, database, etc.) and how it is retrieved (all entries, search, etc.) vary by implementation.
Past chat
Yesterday: asked to fix a test
- Wanted to run it with pytest
- Cause: range bounds
- Instruction: "Write comments
in Japanese"
①
Write out
Memory (external storage)
Run tests with pytest
Watch the range bounds
Write comments in Japanese
②
Load back
New context
Memory: run with pytest /
comments in Japanese
Message: another test fails too,
please fix it.
Remembering ≠ learning.

after.title: Supplement: Latest developments in long-task capability
after.content:
Supplement: Latest developments in long-task capability
METR measures the 50% time horizon of frontier public models at ~12 hours (Feb–Mar 2026). Values over 16 hours are not reliable with the current task suite.
What changed
Item
Update
Date
50% time horizon
~12 hours for the best public models (ranges 5–61 hours). The length of tasks, measured in human working time, that a model has a 50% chance of completing successfully.
Evaluated 2026/2–3
80% time horizon
~1.5 hours at the same point (ranges 50 min–2 h 40 min). Requiring a higher success rate greatly reduces the task length
Evaluated 2026/2–3
Measurement limits
GPT-5.6 Sol estimated at ~11.3 hours. Counting solutions obtained by cheating as successes gives over 270 hours; METR deemed this not a robust measurement
2026/6/26
Link to the lecture: “95% per step, ~36% over 20 steps” was a hypothetical example in the explanation, but real measurements also show a huge gap  between 50% and 80%. Running for a long time and finishing reliably are different things.
Caveats: The time horizon measures task length, not how long a model can run nonstop. The Claude Opus 5.5 evaluation summary (2026/9/22) gives no time-horizon figures.
Source: METR “Frontier Risk Report (February to March 2026)” (2026/5/19), “Summary of METR's predeployment evaluation of GPT-5.6 Sol” (2026/6/26), “Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models” (updated 2026/5/8). Information checked: 2026/10/9

after.title: Supplement: Latest developments in config file standards (AGENTS.md, Skills)
after.content:
Supplement: Latest developments in config file standards (AGENTS.md, Skills)
Shared formats across tools are spreading: AGENTS.md for instruction files, Agent Skills for bundled procedures.
What changed
Item
Update
Date
AGENTS.md
Donated by OpenAI to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation. Adopted by 60,000+ public projects
2025/12/9
Claude Code support
In repositories without CLAUDE.md, reads AGENTS.md directly as instructions (v2.1.277+)
Docs as of 2026/10
Agent Skills
A folder format containing SKILL.md. Only the name and description are read first; the body is read when needed. Skills API out of beta on the Claude API
2026/8/19
Link to the lecture: Side note on the part “config files are also instructions to the model.” Such files are converging on AGENTS.md, which Claude Code can now read.
Caveats: Common formats make it easier to import outside instructions. Read others' AGENTS.md or Skills before letting them inside the boundary.
Source: Linux Foundation announcement of the Agentic AI Foundation (2025/12/9), official AGENTS.md and Agent Skills websites, Anthropic “Claude Platform release notes” (2026/8/19), “How Claude remembers your project”. Information checked: 2026/10/9

after.title: Skill: save the procedure for a repeated task as files
after.content:
Skill: save the procedure for a repeated task as files
Memory stores “what happened.” A Skill stores “how to do it.”
Source: Anthropic, “Agent Skills” and “Skill authoring best practices” (Claude Platform Docs). Token counts are approximate. The Skill shown is a fictional example.
Inside a Skill (example: writing a weekly report)
weekly-report/
SKILL.md　← the steps
template.docx　← template
scripts/collect.py　← tallies data
---
name: weekly-report
description: Use when writing a weekly report
---
1. Collect this week's tickets
2. Write a report using template.docx
① Only the name and description go into context
About 100 tokens each. The body isn't loaded, so context stays light
② Loaded when a request needs the Skill
Only now does the body explaining the steps enter the context.
